subject: Renewal: Surge hedge + 12-month rate-lock proposal
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@brightloop.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-18T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal: Surge hedge + 12-month rate-lock proposal

Hi Ellen —

Great speaking with you this morning. As promised, I pulled together a pragmatic renewal structure that addresses BrightLoop's desire for: a short-term surge protection, a firm unit price for the next 12 months, and optional capacity uplifts tied to a commit ladder.

Key points in the attached workbook (Redwood_Renewal_Hedge_Pricing_v1.xlsx):
- 12-month rate-lock on current per-token price for committed baseline (50M tokens/month).
- Surge hedge: ability to burst up to 200% of baseline at a capped overage rate (15% premium) for two quarters.
- Upsell ladder: incremental discounts (3% / 5%) when moving to 75M and 100M committed tiers respectively, with a 6-month notice window.
- One-time onboarding credit of $25k to offset migration of evaluation workloads into Dedicated.

I included a draft SOW amendment for the uplift and a sample DocuSign workflow to capture the commit. Ben — I looped you for capacity/ops feasibility and for a quick check of the burst pricing math.

Next steps we discussed: BrightLoop to review; if acceptable, we prepare an amendment and route for signatures before the end of the quarter. Can you confirm timing on your side?

Thanks,

Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): Redwood_Renewal_Hedge_Pricing_v1.xlsx, SOW_amendment_draft.pdf

From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@brightloop.io>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Joshi <samir@brightloop.io>
Date: 2028-03-18T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: Surge hedge + 12-month rate-lock proposal

Stephanie —

Thanks for the clear summary and the workbook. High level reaction from our side: the rate-lock for 12 months is appealing; the surge hedge concept meets our needs for Q2/ Q3 expected traffic spikes. A couple of clarifying questions before we escalate to procurement: 

1) Is the 15% overage premium a hard cap for the two-quarter window or can it be negotiated down with a higher baseline commit?
2) The onboarding credit is helpful — does that require any incremental minimums on our side?
3) Will the DocuSign route include line-item visibility for per-token rates both for baseline and burst usage?

We can do a short sync tomorrow if helpful. Samir and I will review the workbook today and circle back with marked changes.

Best,
Ellen Park
Head of Platform Engineering, BrightLoop
ellen.park@brightloop.io

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-18T12:35:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal: Surge hedge + 12-month rate-lock proposal

Steph —

Quick ops check after scanning the workbook:
- Baseline 50M tokens/month on Dedicated is fine; we can commit a node pool that covers that with predictable latency.
- Burst to 100M sustained for short windows is possible, but backing that with a 15% premium only holds if we reserve extra burst capacity in the quarter (otherwise burst is priced at on-demand). We could offer a staged decline: 12% premium if they move to 75M baseline, 10% if 100M baseline.
- The $25k onboarding credit is doable; recommend tying it to a 12-month minimum commitment to preserve economics.

If you want, I can generate a few scenarios (A/B/C) with cost to Redwood and net ARR impact. Marcus — any red flags from infra?

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@brightloop.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-19T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: Surge hedge + 12-month rate-lock proposal

Ellen —

Thanks, this is helpful. Answers inline below and I attached a revised workbook (tab: Options A/B/C) with the staged-premium idea Ben suggested.

1) Premium cap: We can structure it as a hard cap for the two-quarter hedge window only if BrightLoop moves to the 75M baseline (Option B). Otherwise the cap is an aspirational cap and actual on-demand overage rates could apply.

2) Onboarding credit: $25k credit is conditional on a 12-month committed baseline. We can split the credit: $10k applied up front, $15k applied after month 3 contingent on usage migrating.

3) DocuSign: Yes — the amendment will include explicit line items for baseline rate, burst cap rate, and the ladder discounts. Procurement usually wants that detail; we'll make sure the signed amendment contains per-token examples for common monthly usage bands.

Proposed next steps:
- BrightLoop to confirm preferred option (A: conservative baseline + higher burst premium; B: 75M baseline + 12mo rate-lock + 12% burst premium; C: 100M baseline, 10% burst premium + larger discount).
- If B or C chosen, we’ll produce a redline-ready SOW amendment and a DocuSign envelope.

Ellen — can you confirm preferred option by end of day Monday? If procurement needs an internal justification doc, Ben/Marcus and I can draft a short note explaining the tradeoffs.

Cheers,
Stephanie
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): Redwood_Renewal_Hedge_Pricing_v1.xlsx (updated)

From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@brightloop.io>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Joshi <samir@brightloop.io>
Date: 2028-03-20T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: Surge hedge + 12-month rate-lock proposal

Stephanie / Ben —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the options workbook. After running the numbers with Samir, BrightLoop is inclined to pursue Option B (75M baseline). The reasoning: predictable monthly cost, lower effective overage, and the staged onboarding credit helps with our migration budget. Two quick asks before we sign: 

• Can you add a one-time safety clause that lets us temporarily request an extra burst pool during product launches (with 48-hour notice) at the agreed capped premium?
• Procurement will want the DocuSign envelope to include the milestone language for the $15k contingent portion.

If you can update the amendment with those two items, we should be able to route internally and sign next week. Appreciate the team moving quickly on this.

Best,
Ellen
Head of Platform Engineering, BrightLoop
